'''Axel Schumacher''' (born June 14, 1969), is a German [[epigenetics]] researcher. He invented the first [[Comparative genomic hybridization|microarray]] technologies for epigenetic biomarker discovery, developed the ''[[Epigenetic clock|epigenetic theory of aging]]'' with his research leading to the worldwide first proof of whole genome epigenetic abnormalities in Alzheimer's disease.

Alongside his work as a scientist he is a published author, a [[futurologist]] and as of July 2017, CEO and co-founder of the HLTH.network.

== Early life and education ==
Schumacher was born in [[Kreuztal]], Germany in 1969. Schumacher was awarded with a PhD in biology from [[University of Cologne]] under the supervision of {{ill|Robert Koch Prize|de|Robert-Koch-Preis}} laureate {{ill|Walter Doerfler|de}} in 2002.

== Career ==
=== Epigenetics ===
Schumacher started his career in [[epigenetics]] as a visiting researcher at the laboratory of [[Wolf Reik]] at the [[Babraham Institute]] near Cambridge, England working on DNA methylation and [[genomic imprinting]].

During his career he made several breakthrough discoveries including, how genomic imprinting is regulated by DNA methylation,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schumacher|first1=Axel|last2=Buiting|first2=Karin|last3=Zeschnigk|first3=Michael|last4=Doerfler|first4=Walter|last5=Horsthemke|first5=Bernhard|date=August 1998|title=Methylation analysis of the PWS/AS region does not support an enhancer-competition model|journal=Nature Genetics|language=en|volume=19|issue=4|pages=324–325|doi=10.1038/1211|pmid=9697691|s2cid=28353445|issn=1546-1718|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schumacher|first1=A.|last2=Koetsier|first2=P. A.|last3=Hertz|first3=J.|last4=Doerfler|first4=W.|date=2000-12-01|title=Epigenetic and genotype-specific effects on the stability of de novo imposed methylation patterns in transgenic mice|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=275|issue=48|pages=37915–37921|doi=10.1074/jbc.M004839200|issn=0021-9258|pmid=10954710|doi-access=free}}</ref> the effect of in vitro manipulation on imprinted regions in the genome,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schumacher|first1=Axel|last2=Doerfler|first2=Walter|date=2004|title=Influence of in vitro manipulation on the stability of methylation patterns in the Snurf/Snrpn-imprinting region in mouse embryonic stem cells|journal=Nucleic Acids Research|volume=32|issue=4|pages=1566–1576|doi=10.1093/nar/gkh322|issn=1362-4962|pmid=15004243|pmc=390307}}</ref> the first description of 'epigenetic SNPs',<ref>{{Cite M.|last7=Förstl|first7=Hans|last8=Kurz|first8=Alexander|last9=Riemenschneider|first9=Matthias|date=November 2007|title=No association of chromatin-modifying protein 2B with sporadic frontotemporal epigenomics,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kantlehner|first1=Martin|last2=Kirchner|first2=Roland|last3=Hartmann|first3=Petra|last4=Ellwart|first4=Joachim W.|last5=Alunni-Fabbroni|first5=Marianna|last6=Schumacher|first6=Axel|date=April 2011|title=A high-throughput DNA methylation analysis of a single cell|journal=Nucleic Acids Research|volume=39|issue=7|pages=e44|doi=10.1093/nar/gkq1357|issn=0305-1048|pmc=3074158|pmid=21266484}}</ref> with his research leading to the world's first proof of whole genome epigenetic abnormalities in Alzheimer's disease,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Sun-Chong|last2=Oelze|first2=Beatrice|last3=Schumacher|first3=Axel|date=2008-07-16|title=Age-specific epigenetic drift in late-onset Alzheimer's disease|journal=PLOS ONE|volume=3|issue=7|article-number=e2698|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0002698|issn=1932-6203|pmc=2444024|pmid=18628954|bibcode=2008PLoSO...3.2698W |doi-access=free}}</ref> indicating that the main predisposing factors for Alzheimer's disease, [[PSEN1|PSEN]] and [[Apolipoprotein E|APOE]], have a high interindividual variation in humans, which Schumacher invented the technology of 'epigenetic microarrays',<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schumacher|first1=Axel |last2=Kapranov|first2=Philipp|last3=Kaminsky|first3=Zachary|last4=Flanagan|first4=James|last5=Assadzadeh|first5=Abbas|last6=Yau|first6=Patrick|last7=Virtanen|first7=Carl|last8=Winegarden|first8=Neil|last9=Cheng|first9=Jill|last10=Gingeras|first10=Thomas|last11=Petronis|first11=Arturas|date=2006|title=Microarray-based DNA methylation profiling: technology and applications|journal=Nucleic Acids Research|volume=34|issue=2|pages=528–542|doi=10.1093/nar/gkj461|issn=1362-4962|pmc=1345696|pmid=16428248}}</ref> a technology that transformed the research field and led to hundreds of research discoveries across the world, including the first worldwide proof of whole genome epigenetic changes in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mill|first1=Jonathan|last2=Tang|first2=Thomas |last3=Kaminsky|first3=Zachary|last4=Khare|first4=Tarang|last5=Yazdanpanah|first5=Simin|last6=Bouchard|first6=Luigi|last7=Jia|first7=Peixin|last8=Assadzadeh|first8=Abbas|last9=Flanagan|first9=James|last10=Schumacher|first10=Axel |last11=Wang|first11=Sun-Chong|date=March 2008|title=Epigenomic profiling reveals DNA-methylation changes associated with major psychosis|journal=American Journal of Human Genetics|volume=82|issue=3|pages=696–711|doi=10.1016/j.ajhg.2008.01.008|issn=1537-6605|pmc=2427301|pmid=18319075}}</ref>

In 2010, Schumacher proposed the 'epigenetic theory of aging' a new unifying model of aging and the development of complex diseases, incorporating classical aging theories and epigenetics.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Schumacher|first=Axel|title=Handbook of Epigenetics: The New Molecular and Medical Genetics|year=2010|isbn=978-0-12-375709-8|pages=405–422|publisher=Academic }}</ref> His work on epigenetic drift and age-related epigenetic changes in mice and humans<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Schumacher|first=Axel|date=Jan 2009|title=An epigenetic clock: Anticorrelation & DNA methylation as biomarker for aging.|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344399255|journal=ResearchGate}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wang|first1=Sun-Chong|last2=Oelze|first2=Beatrice|last3=Schumacher|first3=Axel|date=2008-07-16|title=Age-specific epigenetic drift in late-onset Alzheimer's disease|journal=PLOS ONE|volume=3|issue=7|article-number=e2698|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0002698|issn=1932-6203|pmc=2444024|pmid=18628954|bibcode=2008PLoSO...3.2698W |doi-access=free}}</ref> laid the foundation to the [[epigenetic clock]] theory of aging.

=== Other work ===
During the 1990s, Schumacher worked as comic book author and artist.<ref>{{cite web|title=Axel Schumacher|url=https://www.lambiek.net/artists/s/schumacher_axel.htm|access-date=2021-08-17|website=lambiek.net|language=en}}</ref> Among others he worked alongside famous artists such as Russian painter Oleg Yudin<ref>{{cite web|title=High Speed (2000) issue OGN SC vol. 01.|url=https://comicbookcollect.com/id367959/|access-date=2021-08-17|website=comicbookcollect.com|language=en-US}}</ref> on titles such as 'High Speed'<ref>{{cite web|title=Oleg Yudin|url=https://www.lambiek.net/artists/y/yudin_oleg.htm|access-date=2021-08-17|website=lambiek.net|language=en}}</ref> and on various stories for the American science fiction and fantasy comics magazine ''[[Heavy Metal (magazine)|Heavy Metal]]''.
